title: Summer upwelling, wind jet and cold filament off southern Vietnam
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

paper.title: Summer upwelling in the South China Sea and its role in regional climate variations

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: The southwest monsoon forms a wind jet off the southern tip of Indochina whose strong wind-stress curl drives coastal and open-ocean upwelling.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'a strong wind jet occurs at its southern tip offshore east of Saigon, resulting in strong wind curls that are important for ocean upwelling off the coast'.
criteria.how_to_test: July-August mean wind speed and wind-stress curl off southern Vietnam (2003-2020 and 2011-2020); jet position; relation between the curl and CMOMS upwelling (cold anomaly, isotherm shoaling).
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: jet latitude +/-0.5 degree; curl sign exact)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: Wind-stress and curl computation from the monthly winds (drag formula stated); a filament index; filament and wind-maximum latitudes; a chlorophyll collocation measure; semi-annual harmonic and variance analysis.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: Model SST and chlorophyll versus satellite data; blended winds versus the paper's scatterometer winds; ten summers; the paper's 1998 example lies outside the period.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
